# Paths, and what flong's two readers of a declaration say of them: the
# launcher (the Zig in tests/zig/paths.zig, through the functions it runs)
# and module.nix's mirrors, which refuse at evaluation what the launcher
# would refuse at launch (DESIGN.md, "Tests": mirrors of the spec in Nix). One
# declaration each, read by both; module.nix asserts its own verdicts
# against this file.
#
# One case a line, its fields separated by a tab:
#
#   CHECK  VERDICT  MIRROR  PATH [PATH]
#
#   CHECK    clean      the spec's clean() of an absolute path
#                       (src/spec.zig; flong-spec.c:203-229) against
#                       module.nix's `clean`
#            overlaps   whether two paths are the same or one lies inside
#                       the other: mount.overlaps (flong-mount.c:82-92), on
#                       the paths as given, against module.nix's `overlaps`
#                       of their `norm`s, as its protected-path check calls
#                       it
#            twice      whether two destinations are the same one, which
#                       the mount helper refuses (mount.sortRefusingTwice;
#                       flong-mount.c:533-541) against module.nix's `twiceIn`
#   VERDICT  yes or no: the launcher's
#   MIRROR   same: module.nix says the same; differs: it says the
#            opposite, by design. The module is lexical and the launcher
#            works on canonical paths (module.nix:128-130): the launcher
#            is given realpath's spelling, the module the declaration's.
#
# Blank lines and lines starting with # are not cases.

# clean
clean	yes	same	/a
clean	yes	same	/a/b
clean	yes	same	/home/u/.cache/flong
clean	yes	same	/...
clean	yes	same	/a b/c
clean	yes	same	/.a/b.
clean	yes	same	/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
clean	no	same	/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
clean	yes	same	/x/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa/y
clean	no	same	/
clean	no	same	
clean	no	same	a
clean	no	same	a/b
clean	no	same	//a
clean	no	same	/a//b
clean	no	same	/a/
clean	no	same	/.
clean	no	same	/..
clean	no	same	/a/.
clean	no	same	/a/./b
clean	no	same	/a/../b
clean	no	same	/a/..
# PATH_MAX: the launcher refuses a path of 4096 bytes or more; the module has no such bound.
clean	no	differs	
clean	yes	same	
# overlaps
overlaps	yes	same	/a	/a
overlaps	yes	same	/a	/a/b
overlaps	yes	same	/a/b	/a
overlaps	no	same	/a	/ab
overlaps	no	same	/ab	/a
overlaps	no	same	/a/b	/a/c
overlaps	no	same	/run/user/1000	/run/user/100
overlaps	yes	same	/run/user/1000/flong	/run/user/1000
# / holds everything to the launcher; the module's lexical compare says no, and refuses a source of / by its own rule (reachesManager).
overlaps	yes	differs	/	/a
overlaps	yes	differs	/a	/
overlaps	yes	same	/	/
# The module compares the spelling it normalises; the launcher, given canonical paths, never meets these spellings.
overlaps	no	differs	//a	/a
overlaps	no	differs	/a/	/a/b
overlaps	no	differs	/var/run/user/1000	/run/user/1000
overlaps	no	differs	/var/run	/run/user
# twice
twice	yes	same	/srv/work	/srv/work
twice	no	same	/srv/work	/srv/work/x
twice	no	same	/srv/work	/srv/wor
twice	no	same	/a	/b
twice	no	same	/a b	/a
